correctness.rationale: The basis realizes an RKHS: local square summability gives bounded point evaluation and locally uniform convergence, and its nonzero diagonal Taylor coefficients give injectivity. On the domain of D, the factorization B=(I+aSD⁻¹)D is valid; the norm of (SD⁻¹)^k is 1/k!, so the inverse series converges for every complex a. The commutator BS−SB=S gives the bounded multiplier S−B⁻¹S, first on finite coefficient sequences and then by continuity of evaluations. Triangular inversion gives the coefficient of f_(n+j) in z^n as (−a)^j n!/(n+j+1)!; at aligned indices the coefficients for z^n are −a/(n+1) times those for z^(n+1), with the stated first-slot-linear convention. Polynomials are in the space and dense since each basis vector is a polynomial. Beta moments on [0,1] squared and summed by Tonelli give the law of the product of the two integration variables, with Jacobian 1/t: its density is rho_a and its moments are m_n. A subnormal extension gives a positive scalar spectral measure at the cyclic vector 1; m_n→0 puts it in the disk with no unit-circle mass. Hausdorff uniqueness fixes its radial pushforward. The pushed-forward complex measure weighted by conjugate z has moments −a m_(n+1)/(n+1), which by Fubini and polynomial density uniquely fix its density to −a∫_q^1 rho_a(t)dt. Its variation must be dominated by √q rho_a(q)dq. The left density in absolute value approaches |a|m_0>0 for a≠0 but the bound is at most I_0(2|a|)√q log(1/q)→0, contradicting almost-everywhere domination on a whole interval. For a=0 the rotational measure with radial squared-modulus density −log q gives the exact diagonal moments and vanishing off-diagonal ones; the monomial isometry realizes normal multiplication as an extension.
